headline: Week seven: block peak banked, calf passes its trail test
narrative: Block peak, and the number is banked — a small surplus on the biggest target of the block, with time on feet essentially on the ask. The centrepiece was Friday's Hope/Edale loop: Lose Hill, Back Tor, Hollins Cross, Mam Tor, Lord's Seat, Grindslow Knoll — the heaviest single day of climbing in the build so far. Around it sat midweek hiking reps on Mellor Moor and a Sunday trail run over Higher Moor. The one honest miss: the brief asked for the first back-to-back, hike Saturday and descend Sunday, and Saturday went to a walked parkrun instead. The volume is done; the B2B rehearsal isn't, and it now belongs to the Build weeks.

The calf earned its first mention in weeks — a good one. Tuesday's Alderley club trail run put real running pace through it and it didn't blow up, in the day's own notes. Seven weeks without a setback, and now one with a proper test passed. Week eight is a deload with the Effer check on run reintroduction: undershooting is the job, so let the block peak soak in — overshooting the target is what failure looks like on a recovery week.
